page: Amazon Web Services c7g.xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. Built on the 64-bit ARMv8 architecture with Neoverse-V1 cores, this instance features 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs running at 2.6 GHz, with no hyperthreading. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, features a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps, and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results indicate balanced performance for standard computing tasks, alongside notable limitations in specialized workloads. The c7g.xlarge achieves average performance in stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests, as well as in Geekbench software compilation and text processing. However, the ARM-based architecture shows performance trade-offs in cryptographic and complex mathematical operations. Passmark CPU encryption tests place the instance in the bottom 10% with a score of 548.88, while Passmark CPU extended instructions and Geekbench ray tracing and image processing benchmarks fall into the bottom 25%. LLM inference speeds are also limited, with text generation on a medium 7B model reaching only 5.99 tokens per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c7g.xlarge offers a resource-dense compute profile for workloads that do not require high memory allocations or local storage. It is highly suitable for static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 8.02 GB/sec, and in-memory key-value stores, demonstrating 6.65 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. The instance is also well-suited for database operations and general utility computing. It is less appropriate for memory-intensive applications, cryptographic processing, or machine learning inference.

It is configured with 8.0 GB of memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per-core ratio, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps without local storage or GPU accelerators.
